## Goal

Batch work (audit and plan/intake child dispatch) must identify itself with an explicit `X-Priority` header so the proxy's priority routing can tell it apart from interactive sessions; today every request arrives with no priority header (`header=(none)`) and, during the cheap window, is treated as `low` alongside the interactive panes it competes with.

## Problem statement

During the 2026-11-03 incident window (08:30–09:10 local, inside the default cheap window), five audit subprocesses plus a plan run competed with interactive herdr panes for one GPU. Every routing decision logged `priority_decision priority=low header=(none)`: priority routing had no client signal to act on, so batch and interactive traffic were indistinguishable. Batch work should declare itself so interactive sessions can be preferred whenever the routing policy permits it.

## Users

- **Operator of an interactive herdr pane** — wants the agent session they are actively typing into to stay responsive while batch audit/plan jobs run.
- **Downtime/batch dispatcher** — wants batch jobs to be schedulable at lower priority without starving.
- **Proxy maintainer** — wants an attributable, documented client contract (`header=` in the log) instead of guessing from timing.

User stories:

- As an operator typing in a herdr pane, I want my session served ahead of background audit/plan work so the UI does not stall behind a 7-minute prefill.
- As a batch dispatcher, I want my subprocesses to advertise `low` priority so they queue/park instead of competing as equals with interactive work.
- As a proxy maintainer, I want the priority of every request attributable in `proxy.log` (`priority_decision priority=… header=…`).

## Evidence (incident 2026-11-03)

- `proxy.log` 08:30–09:10: every `priority_decision` line recorded `priority=low header=(none)` for interactive panes, audit subprocesses and plan children alike.
- The window falls inside the default cheap window (`server.priority_window` 01:00–10:00 local), which caps **every** request to `low` regardless of header.

## Acceptance Criteria

Provisional — AC1–AC3 follow the existing item text; AC-A1/AC-A2 record the assumptions pending producer answers (see Appendix).

- AC1: The batch dispatch paths — audit `_call_pi` and the plan/intake child dispatch (and any herdr downtime batch launch) — send an explicit priority header on every model call. The value is `low` (the "batch" tier) unless the producer answers otherwise (AC-A1). The request appears in `proxy.log` as `priority_decision priority=low header=low`.
- AC2: Interactive herdr panes do **not** set the batch header; their requests log `header=(none)` (effective `medium` outside the cheap window). A test with two concurrent sessions (one batch `low`, one interactive default) demonstrates the interactive request is preferred under contention when the cheap window is disabled.
- AC3: Invalid/unknown `X-Priority` values fall back to the default (`medium`) with a warning rather than erroring; the batch-header contract (how a client sends it) is documented in the proxy config docs.
- AC4: A regression test covers (a) the batch dispatch helper emitting the header and (b) the proxy recording it in `priority_decision`; the existing server-side parsing/validation tests remain green.
- AC5: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- AC6: Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Interactive sessions can be distinguished from batch audit/plan work in the proxy's routing decisions, so an actively-used pane no longer competes as an equal with background jobs whenever the routing policy permits preference.

## Constraints

- **Proxy vocabulary is `low|medium|high` only** (`proxy/proxy/priority.py`). `batch` is not a valid header value — an unknown value falls back to `medium`, which would *defeat* the purpose. `low` is the natural batch tier (prefer local, queue, avoid paid remote).
- **Cheap window caps everything to `low`** (`server.priority_window`, default 01:00–10:00 local, `enabled: true` in `proxy/config.yaml`). During that window a batch header cannot protect interactive sessions — the incident occurred inside it. This is the central open question (AC-A2).
- **No trust gate yet.** Any reachable client may claim any priority (`LP-0MVDTE0CI0088QOR` tracks hardening). Batch only needs to claim `low`, so this is not blocking.
- **Cross-repo client wiring.** The proxy (this repo) already parses `X-Priority`; the missing piece is on the client side. `pi` has no `--header` CLI flag; provider headers come from `models.json` (`$NAME` env interpolation, docs/models-configuration.md). The audit/plan/intake dispatch and interactive herdr panes live in SorraAgents skills and the herdr dispatcher, not in this repo.
- Do not edit `~/.pi/` or agent-infrastructure outside this repo without an explicit owning work item.

## Existing state

- `proxy/proxy/priority.py` — full server-side priority vocabulary, cheap window, effective priority, request stamping, provider chains.
- `proxy/proxy/ui.py` (~line 1275) — computes effective priority per request and logs `priority_decision priority=%s header=%s`.
- `proxy/tests/test_priority_routing.py` — covers parsing, absent/invalid → medium, cheap window, `X-Priority-Applied`.
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` and `proxy/README.md` — document `X-Priority` and `priority_window` (server contract).
- `~/.pi/agent/models.json` / SorraAgents `.pi-config/agent/models.json` — `Local Proxy` provider has no `headers` block today.
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py::_call_pi` — builds `pi_env = scrub_repository_overrides(os.environ)` and launches `pi -p --mode json …`; `priority` there is a **local queue** priority, not an HTTP header.
- `pi` client — sets identity/session-affinity headers; no `X-Priority` support and no `PI_PRIORITY` env convention.

## Desired change

1. Define the batch contract: `X-Priority: low` sent by batch dispatch paths (config/env-driven, no per-call code duplication).
2. Wire the client: `models.json` provider `headers` maps `X-Priority` to an env var (e.g. `$PI_PRIORITY`); batch launch paths set that env var, interactive panes do not.

```jsonc
// SorraAgents/.pi-config/agent/models.json (and live ~/.pi/agent/models.json)
"Local Proxy": {
  "api": "openai-completions",
  "baseUrl": "http://192.168.0.199:8000/v1",
  "apiKey": "not_needed",
  "headers": { "X-Priority": "$PI_PRIORITY" },   // unset/empty → proxy default (medium)
  "compat": { "sendSessionAffinityHeaders": true },
  "models": [{ "id": "plan" }, { "id": "code" }, { "id": "author" }]
}
```

```bash
# Batch dispatch (audit _call_pi, plan/intake children, herdr downtime panes)
PI_PRIORITY=low pi -p --mode json --model code "$PROMPT"

# Interactive herdr pane — no env var, so header is absent/empty (→ medium)
pi
```
3. Document the client contract in `proxy/docs/routing.md` / `proxy/README.md` with a copy-paste example.
4. Add regression tests for header emission (client helper, unit) and the `priority_decision` log line (proxy, integration), and keep the existing invalid-value fallback test.
5. Record the cheap-window limitation and the ownership split (see Appendix).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/docs/routing.md` — Needs a "Sending priority from a client (batch vs interactive)" subsection and the cheap-window caveat.
- `proxy/README.md` — Needs the client header contract next to the existing `X-Priority` bullet (~line 1306).

  - `SorraAgents/skill/plan/` + `SorraAgents/skill/intake/` — set the env var on child dispatch.
  - `SorraAgents/.pi-config/agent/models.json` (and live `~/.pi/agent/models.json`) — add `"headers": {"X-Priority": "$PI_PRIORITY"}` to the `Local Proxy` provider.
  - herdr downtime dispatcher — set the env var for batch panes, leave interactive panes untouched.

## Related work

- `LP-0MVDT94F0003VHUA` — Priority-based routing replacing fast/cheap mode (completed): introduced `X-Priority`, `priority_window`, provider `priorities`.
- `LP-0MVDTE0CI0088QOR` — Priority header trust gate (open): spoofing hardening; orthogonal because batch claims `low`.
- `LP-0MVGPZWY0001JD1D` — Per-provider `priorities` (completed): the server-side chain filter this header feeds.
- `LP-0MPOOT5P3007CZLF` / `LP-0MTXEED8E003EDM8` / `LP-0MQ5BMQTH0019IOY` — automated related-work report (see the regenerated section below).
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` — priority routing reference; `proxy/README.md` — client header bullet.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk (high): the cheap window defeats the feature during cheap hours.** Every request is capped to `low` 01:00–10:00 local, which is exactly when the incident happened. If "protect interactive sessions" must hold at all times, this item needs a cheap-window policy change (see AC-A2), which is a routing-policy decision, not a header-plumbing change.
- **Risk (medium): header interpolation when the env var is unset.** `"$PI_PRIORITY"` must resolve to an empty/absent header for interactive panes (→ default `medium`), not an error. Verify against the installed pi version before relying on it; fall back to a provider-extension or wrapper if it errors.
- **Risk (medium): scope creep into other repos.** The client wiring lives in SorraAgents/herdr. Recording it here without an owning item risks an unimplementable LP item. See AC-A3.
- **Assumption:** "batch" in AC1 means the `low` priority tier, not a literal `batch` header value (AC-A1).
- **Assumption:** AC2's contention test disables `priority_window` so the comparison is meaningful (AC-A2).
- **Scope-creep note:** a trust gate (`LP-0MVDTE0CI0088QOR`) and any cheap-window policy change are separate items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

### OPEN QUESTION — AC-A1: Which priority value should batch work send?

- **Q:** The proxy vocabulary is `low|medium|high`; a literal `X-Priority: batch` would be rejected and fall back to `medium` (defeating the purpose). Which value should batch dispatch send?
  - (a) `low` — prefer local, queue, avoid paid remote; no proxy change. **Recommended.**
  - (b) Add a `batch` alias in `proxy/proxy/priority.py` mapped to `low` (proxy vocabulary change + tests).
  - (c) `medium` — same as today's default; no differentiation. Not recommended.
- **Answer:** OPEN QUESTION. **Recommended:** (a) `low` — it already means "prefer local, queue, avoid paid", matches batch semantics, and avoids widening the proxy vocabulary.
- **Research:** `proxy/proxy/priority.py` `VALID_PRIORITIES = ("low", "medium", "high")`; `parse_priority` warns and returns `medium` for unknown values. `priority_routing_profile` gives `low` → queue + local economic bypass. `proxy/tests/test_priority_routing.py` covers invalid → medium.

### OPEN QUESTION — AC-A2: How should interactive sessions be protected during the cheap window?

- **Q:** The default cheap window (01:00–10:00 local) caps **every** request to `low`, including interactive panes, so a batch header cannot differentiate them during the incident's hours. What is the intended behaviour?
  - (a) Accept the limitation: batch header protects interactive only outside the cheap window; document it. **Recommended (smallest change).**
  - (b) Exempt `high` from the cheap-window cap so interactive panes can send `high` and win even during cheap hours (proxy routing-policy change + tests).
  - (c) Disable or narrow `priority_window` (operator config change).
- **Answer:** OPEN QUESTION. **Recommended:** (a) — document the limitation; changing the cap is a routing-policy decision that should be its own item if desired.
- **Research:** `proxy/proxy/priority.py::effective_priority` returns `low` unconditionally inside the window; `proxy/config.yaml` `priority_window.enabled: true`, `start: "01:00"`, `end: "10:00"`. The incident (08:30–09:10) is inside this window.

### OPEN QUESTION — AC-A3: Which repo owns the client-side wiring?

- **Q:** The proxy already parses `X-Priority`; the missing changes are client-side: audit `_call_pi`, plan/intake child dispatch, `models.json` provider headers, and the herdr dispatcher. These live in SorraAgents and herdr, not in this `llm-manager` repo. How should the work be split?
  - (a) Split: keep this LP item for the proxy-side contract, docs and tests; create linked SorraAgents (and herdr, if needed) items for the client wiring. **Recommended.**
  - (b) Let this LP item carry the cross-repo changes (needs explicit cross-repo authorisation).
- **Answer:** OPEN QUESTION. **Recommended:** (a) split — keeps each item implementable in its own repo/worktree and avoids an LP item whose code cannot land here.
- **Research:** `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py::_call_pi` (SorraAgents) builds `pi_env`; `SorraAgents/.pi-config/agent/models.json` `Local Proxy` provider has no `headers`; `pi` exposes no `--header` flag (`pi --help`).

# Local admission over-prices a live occupant by its adaptive *lease ceiling*, refusing pinned requests that would be served in seconds

discovered-from:LP-0MWKWGLRT003AUG4

## Impact

Operators' locally-pinned (herdr-dispatched) requests intermittently fail with `429 Local admission refused` while the GPU is mid-prefill of another request that is about to finish — the proxy quotes a 5-minute wait for a 3-second occupant.

## Problem statement

With `X-Local-Preference: local-preferred`, a request that **fits** local capacity is never promoted to a paid provider; if the local admission guard refuses it, the client gets a retryable `429 Local admission refused`. Since the orphan-marker wedge was cleared (`LP-0MWKWGLRT003AUG4`, 2026-11-17 16:21) the local route is healthy — 332 local streams served, zero `local_dispatch_denied ... records_total=0` — but refusals continue for a different reason:

```
18:12:56,371 local_admission_guard decision=reject reason=prefill_eta_exceeds_deadline enforced=true
  eta_prefill_s=22.6 eta_occupancy_s=316.9 occupant_hold_s=316.9 projected_wait_s=339.5
  budget_s=30.0 deadline_s=180.0 deadline_budget_s=171.0 new_tokens=49 budget_tokens=25000
  rate_bucket=solitary busy_slots=1 in_flight_prefills=1 gate_occupancy=1 free_slot=true
  session=herdr-1794936961-3759269-19297
18:12:56,371 local_only_refused reason=prefill_eta_exceeds_deadline preference=local-preferred
  verdict=deferrable ... route=refused
```

A **49-new-token** follow-up turn was refused because the single in-flight occupant was priced at
316.9 s. That occupant was `herdr-1794938529-3818195-11862`, dispatched `18:12:54,935`, first byte
`18:12:58,613` — **3.7 s of prefill**, priced as 316.9 s (86x over).

## Root cause

`proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py:_live_prefill_remaining_seconds` (≈3805-3897) sums, per live
prefilling record:

```
max(_occupant_prefill_remaining_seconds(record), _occupant_lease_hold_seconds(record))
```

`_occupant_lease_hold_seconds` (≈3966) returns the record's remaining `expires_at`, which is the
**adaptive dispatch-lease ceiling** from `_get_adaptive_lease_timeout_seconds` (≈1110):

```
adaptive = base_timeout(180 s) + estimated_tokens * local_dispatch_lease_per_token_seconds(0.015)
           capped at local_dispatch_lease_max_seconds(1500)
```

That ceiling is a *retention* bound chosen so a lease never lapses mid-prefill — it is ~4x the
measured prefill rate (`cold_ms_per_token=3.9`, i.e. 0.0039 s/token) plus a 180 s base. Taking
`max()` with it means the guard prices the occupant at its worst-case lease even when its
*measured* remaining service is a second or two, so `projected_wait_s` almost always exceeds
`deadline_budget_s=171 s` whenever a mid-size prompt is in flight.

The two components are known-good in opposite directions: the measured service term
(`_occupant_prefill_remaining_seconds`, `LP-0MVS9YK9P006M1NQ`) re-prices from remaining *uncached*
tokens; the lease-hold term was added by `LP-0MVV29YDQ00437N6` to stop the guard *under*-pricing an
occupant that holds the slot for the whole queue budget (the 2026-10-28 `eta_occupancy_s=16.0`
under-price). The fix must keep the floor without letting the ceiling dominate measured evidence.

## Evidence (2026-11-17, live proxy `/tmp/proxy-startup-20261116T152048Z-3719311.log`)

Refusals since the wedge fix (all `preference=local-preferred`, all `verdict=deferrable`):

| time | session | new_tokens | eta_prefill_s | occupant_hold_s | projected_wait_s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 17:05:11 | herdr-1794935018-… | 55 | 21.2 | 204.6 | 225.8 |
| 17:20:10 | herdr-1794935018-… | 17 | 56.4 | 401.4 | 457.8 |
| 17:36:04 | herdr-1794935018-… | 7578 | 13.9 | 413.8 | 427.7 |
| 18:02:41 | herdr-1794938529-… | 4039 | 9.8 | 327.7 | 337.5 |
| 18:12:56 | herdr-1794936961-… | 49 | 22.6 | 316.9 | 339.5 |

Every one is `free_slot=true`, `in_flight_prefills=1`, against `deadline_budget_s=171.0`.

## Scope

- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`: `_live_prefill_remaining_seconds`,
  `_occupant_lease_hold_seconds`, `_get_adaptive_lease_timeout_seconds` (how the hold ceiling is
  derived/decayed).
- Tests: `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py`, `test_admission_reserve.py`,
  `test_prefill_thrash_wedge.py`, `test_local_dispatch_gate.py`.

Out of scope: the `local-preferred` refusal contract (`LP-0MVSHWL47000EVJY`); client-side handling of
retryable 429 (`WL-0MVSBF5XZ001H7V7`); the orphan-marker wedge (`LP-0MWKWGLRT003AUG4`); lease
*fairness* across renewals (`LP-0MVOJ6KAW004EBV0`).

## Acceptance criteria

1. The occupant term no longer prices a record at its lease ceiling when measured progress says it is
   nearly done: for a record whose measured remaining prefill is `R` seconds, the term is
   `<= max(R * k, floor)` for a documented small `k` and floor (not the raw `expires_at`).
2. Regression pinned to this incident: an in-flight occupant 2 s into a 9k-token prefill (adaptive
   lease ≈317 s, `first_byte_seen=false`) must not refuse a `local-preferred` 49-new-token request
   that fits capacity and whose own prefill fits `deadline_budget_s`; the request is admitted (or
   deferred within `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds`) instead of 429.
3. The under-pricing cure of `LP-0MVV29YDQ00437N6` is preserved: the 2026-10-28 shape (occupant with
   no progress signal, `eta_occupancy_s` collapsing to ~0 as the queue ages) still prices the
   occupant, and its regression tests stay green.
4. Refusal diagnostics become attributable: the guard log exposes the priced components
   (measured service vs lease hold) so an over-priced refusal is provable from one log line.
5. A lease whose holder has already served its first byte, or whose record is inactive, contributes
   nothing to the occupancy term (no regression from the current filter).
6. Full suite green via the test skill.

## Notes

- No live state is stale in this failure mode: `POST /v1/leases/release` and a proxy restart do not
  help, which distinguishes it from the orphan-marker wedge. Do not "clear" it operationally.
- Retryable by contract: the refusal carries `Retry-After` / `retry_at`; the observable pain is that
  a 1-3 s wait is quoted as 5 minutes, so the client gives up or retries into the next large prefill.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MSIC2UJX007C0IR** – Implement adaptive lease for anonymous sessions (completed)
- **LP-0MSJ7W7YE003HETO** – Hermetic tests: prefill-progress lease extension (completed)

## Problem statement

The first proxy-initiated `/slots` poll after a proxy restart can fire
*before* child-port discovery has succeeded, so it takes the router-port
fallback path: it logs a `slots_child_port_unavailable` WARNING
(`model=Qwen3`, `source=log_signal`), increments
`llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total{reason="no_child_port_router_mode"}`
and traverses the router (`:8080`) instead of the model child port.

Consequence: every 24 h post-restart verification window on this surface
starts with a guaranteed chat-model fallback, which fails a zero-tolerance
"chat-model fallback delta == 0" acceptance criterion even when
steady-state operation is clean.

## Evidence (measured, LP-0MVP7HX2S008IU57 window 2026-11-16T15:20:47Z → 2026-11-17T15:20:47Z)

The window is anchored to the proxy restart (`pid 3720326`, `lstart`
2026-11-16T15:20:47Z), so the process-lifetime counter delta *is* the window
delta. In `proxy.log.2026-11-16_15`, immediately after the boot sequence
(`Started TTS server`, `death capture: armed`, `Slot occupancy sampler
started (interval 10.0s)`):

```text
2026-11-16 15:20:51,411 - WARNING - slots_child_port_unavailable: no model child port discovered for model=Qwen3 (source=log_signal); falling back to router port 8080 — every proxy-initiated /slots poll will traverse t...
2026-11-16 15:20:51,435 - WARNING - llama-server --version returned 127
2026-11-16 15:20:51,560 - INFO - Adopted running llama-server (model=router parallel=1 router_mode=True); preserving warm prompt cache
```

- Only **one** `Starting LLama Proxy Server` marker in the whole window
  (15:20:49.786, the anchor process's own boot) ⇒ no in-window restart.
- `llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total{reason="no_child_port_router_mode"}`
  = **1.0** for a process that started at the window start.
- Exactly **one** `slots_child_port_unavailable` line in the window, at
  window start **+4.4 s**; **zero** for the remaining 23 h 59 m 56 s.
- The same transient is visible in the earlier LP-0MVVLKPBM007F6U6 window
  (3 × `model=Qwen3`, each one within 3 s of a restart) — i.e. it is
  restart-correlated, not busy-child-correlated.

## Desired change

Make the boot-time slot poll child-port-aware: either

1. retry/defer the first slot poll until child-port discovery has resolved
   (bounded backoff), or
2. mark the poll as a boot transient so the fallback counter / WARNING are
   not incremented before discovery has had a chance to succeed.

The zero-tolerance signal (`llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total` + the
`slots_child_port_unavailable` WARNING) must stay usable as a *regression*
signal — a boot-time increment makes a clean 24 h window indistinguishable
from one real discovery regression.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** — After a proxy restart, the first proxy-initiated `/slots` poll
  does not increment `llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total{reason="no_child_port_router_mode"}`
  and does not emit `slots_child_port_unavailable` when the model child port
  becomes discoverable within the boot window.
- **AC2** — A genuine discovery regression (child port never discoverable)
  still increments the counter and emits the WARNING; covered by a test.
- **AC3** — Reproduced by a test: boot sequence with a not-yet-ready child
  port ⇒ no fallback counter increment; child port never ready ⇒ counter
  increments once per throttled interval.
- **AC4** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the change.
- **AC5** — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A restarted proxy no longer looks like it had a child-port discovery
regression on its very first slot poll, so a clean 24 h window can pass the
zero-tolerance fallback check.
